edges.reason: msg.sender is used as the sole recipient of DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and every privileged role in the public initialize function; if initialize can be front-run or re-run on a proxy/implementation, an attacker becomes admin.
onlyRole(MINTER_ROLE) gates the minting entry point; the role check is the access-control barrier.
onlyRole(PAUSER_ROLE) gates pause().
onlyRole(PAUSER_ROLE) gates unpause().
onlyRole(UPGRADER_ROLE) gates _authorizeUpgrade, the only barrier protecting the delegatecall upgrade.
The counter's current value is read as the token id argument of _safeMint and then incremented.
Caller-supplied mint recipient flows into safeMint's _safeMint call.
The attacker-controllable recipient address becomes the target of the external onERC721Received callback, enabling reentrant calls during minting.
safeMint performs an external call to the recipient contract via _checkOnERC721Received before returning to the caller.
_msgSender() is forwarded as the operator argument of onERC721Received, coupling caller identity with the untrusted callback.
The new implementation address parameter is consumed by the upgrade authorization hook.
Once authorized, the upgrade routine delegatecalls arbitrary code from the new implementation in the proxy's storage context.
The address supplied to the upgrade becomes the delegatecall target, so weak role control over this parameter means arbitrary code execution in the proxy.
safeMint triggers _beforeTokenTransfer through _safeMint->_mint; the hook reverts the mint while the contract is paused.
from address is passed into the transfer hook.
to address is passed into the transfer hook.
tokenId is passed into the transfer hook.
_burn routes through _beforeTokenTransfer before deleting ownership.
tokenId parameter is burned and its approvals/URI cleared.
tokenId parameter selects the URI mapping entry to return.
tokenURI concatenates the value returned by _baseURI with the stored token URI.

normalization_plan.reason: The recipient parameter only exists as input to safeMint and should be collapsed into that core function node.
from is exclusively consumed by the transfer hook and adds no independent semantics.
to is exclusively consumed by the transfer hook and adds no independent semantics.
tokenId is exclusively consumed by the transfer hook and adds no independent semantics.
The proposed implementation address is only meaningful inside the upgrade authorization routine.
tokenId is only used as the burn target inside _burn.
tokenId only selects the storage lookup performed by tokenURI.
